result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.edge_subgraph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Extract a subgraph containing the specified edges and their endpoint nodes. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L12974-L13038){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.edge_subgraph(edges) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Returns a new graph containing only the specified edges and the nodes that are endpoints of those edges. This is useful when you want to focus on specific relationships rather than specific nodes. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [edges]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : List of edge IDs to include in the subgraph. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : New graph containing only the specified edges and their endpoint nodes. Preserves directedness, weightedness, and node labels. Edge weights are preserved. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If any edge ID is not found in the graph. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Extract specific edges from a graph: ::: {#f925aea9 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec # Create a cycle: 1 -- 2 -- 3 -- 4 -- 5 -- 1 graph = ec.Graph().add_cycle_graph(5) # Get first two edge IDs edge_ids = list(graph.get_edge_ids())[:2] sub = graph.edge_subgraph(edge_ids) # Returns 3 (endpoints of 2 edges) sub.count_nodes() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 3 ``` ::: ::: ::: {#9c2ee924 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Returns 2 sub.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 2 ``` ::: ::: Extract a path from a complete graph: ::: {#fb332e8c .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_full_graph(4) # K4 with 6 edges # Select specific edges to form a path edge_ids = list(graph.get_edge_ids())[:2] path = graph.edge_subgraph(edge_ids) path.count_nodes(), path.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` (3, 2) ``` ::: :::
